SHOW.name: Design showrooms and makers
SHOW.fix: Order to cash on made to order pieces, landed cost, one price book.

DLR.name: Design dealers, galleries and rugs
DLR.fix: One of a kind inventory margin, consignment settlements, fair P&L.

KIT.name: Kitchens, tile and stone
KIT.fix: Project ledger from deposit to install, change orders, inventory truth.

RE.name: Boutique brokerages
RE.fix: Agent production, marketing spend per deal, client facing market pages.

PM.name: Residential property management
PM.fix: Board facing building ledgers, portfolio vendor spend, duplicate invoices.

DEV.name: Boutique developers
DEV.fix: Budget versus committed versus paid across projects, change order exposure.

OWN.name: Owner's reps and luxury builders
OWN.fix: Owner ledger: pay app checks, change orders, schedule. Proven with PGM.

ID.name: Interior design and architecture
ID.fix: Purchasing ledger: deposits versus POs versus received, fee realization.

ART.name: Art galleries
ART.fix: Consignment settlements, multi site inventory, fair and shipping costs.

JEW.name: Independent jewelers
JEW.fix: Memo and custom build tracking, inventory turn and margin per piece.

EVT.name: Event design and florists
EVT.fix: Event P&L quote versus actual, vendor commitments, unbilled overages.

leads.note: Designer cooperative showroom. Dozens of independent designers consign through one storefront, so the money flows are many to one and reconciliations are painful.
leads.fix: Consignment and commission settlement across every designer member, with a clean statement each month and a dashboard the designers can log into.
leads.open: Walk up to the second floor. Open with the monthly settlement run: how many hours and how many spreadsheets.

leads.note: Contemporary gallery, founder led, New York and LA, large fair program. Consignment, shipping, insurance and fair costs on every sale.
leads.fix: Artist consignment settlements, fair P&L and shipping and insurance allocation to sales.
leads.open: Walk in Tue to Sat. Ask for the director. Open with fair P&L.

leads.note: Founder owned Toronto house with a New York showroom in the Design Center. Represents dozens of makers, trade pricing, cross border shipping.
leads.fix: Cross border landed cost and maker payments, trade pricing control, and showroom level sales reporting the founder can read on his phone.
leads.open: Walk in on 28th Street. Open with cross border cost: how often does the quote miss the real landed number.

leads.note: Family owned kitchen designer and dealer with an A&D Building showroom and Westchester showrooms. Every project is a deposit, drawings, orders to cabinet makers, installers and change orders.
leads.fix: Kitchen project ledger: deposits, cabinet maker POs, installer payments and change orders with margin by project.
leads.open: Walk the A&D Building and ask for the showroom manager. Open with change orders: how many per project and who eats them.

leads.note: Family owned multi brand showroom that also runs the Minotti New York flagship at the same address. Multiple brand price lists, trade discounts, big residential and hospitality projects.
leads.fix: Project level margin across brands, discount governance, and a clean customer master across both showrooms.
leads.open: Walk in on Madison. Open with project margin: when a 40 piece residential job closes, who knows the real margin after freight and punch list. One owner covers both brands.

leads.note: Brazilian modern design, founder owned, showrooms in New York, Miami and LA. Imports with long lead times and container freight, trade clients across the country.
leads.fix: Import pipeline: container timing, duties, deposits to Brazilian makers, and client deposits held against them.
leads.open: Walk in. Ask how many client deposits are sitting against pieces still on the water and who tracks the spread.

leads.note: Independent design store and its own Matter Made line. Mix of imported brands and in house production, so landed cost and currency hit every quote.
leads.fix: Landed cost by vendor and currency, inventory that is really on hand versus on order, and a margin by brand view.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with landed cost: do quotes still use last year's freight and exchange rates.

leads.note: Founder owned lighting brand with a SoHo showroom and Brooklyn production. Many SKUs, many finishes, dealers and direct trade sales side by side.
leads.fix: One price book across dealers and direct trade, production lead time truth, and a clean cost per fixture so discounts stop eating the margin.
leads.open: Walk in. Ask how a dealer order and a direct trade order are priced today and who checks that both land on margin.

leads.note: Home furnishings line with a walk in showroom on 59th, alongside the design studio. Wholesale, retail and trade in one business.
leads.fix: Channel margin across wholesale, trade and retail, and inventory by SKU.
leads.open: Walk in to the 59th Street showroom. Open with channel margin.

leads.note: Antique and custom rug gallery, owner led, serves the top designers. Custom orders carry deposits, overseas weaving and long timelines.
leads.fix: Custom rug pipeline from deposit to weaving to delivery, with landed cost and a designer facing status view.
leads.open: Walk in on the 7th floor. Open with how many custom orders are in production and when each was promised.

leads.note: Design gallery with a global artist roster, Design Miami and Basel every year, production financed for artists. Heavy project accounting for a small team.
leads.fix: Production advances to artists tracked against sales, fair level P&L and a clean inventory of editions.
leads.open: Walk in Tue to Sat. Open with artist advances: what is outstanding, against which editions.

leads.note: Founder led gallery with Chelsea spaces, a Tribeca flagship and The School in Kinderhook. Big roster, logistics heavy.
leads.fix: Inventory and loan tracking across four sites, consignment settlements.
leads.open: Walk in.

leads.note: Family owned antiques house since 1939 with thousands of pieces, a rental business for film and events, and sales. Two revenue models on one inventory.
leads.fix: Rental utilization and revenue per piece next to sale margin, plus a vendor master for restorers and shippers.
leads.open: Walk in to the 61st Street galleries. Open with rental utilization by category.

leads.note: Founder led gallery with a Korean and international roster. Small team, fairs, consignments.
leads.fix: Consignment ledger and fair P&L.
leads.open: Walk in. Pair with other Chelsea galleries on one route.

leads.note: Studio contemporary design and vintage dealer, represents artists, big fair presence. Commissions produced for clients with long timelines.
leads.fix: Commission tracking from deposit to delivery and artist settlement, plus fair P&L.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with open commissions: deposits held, production spent, and what is owed to artists.

leads.note: Estate and vintage jewelry house on Madison, family owned by Kwiat. One of a kind inventory, memo to stylists and red carpet loans.
leads.fix: Memo and loan tracking with insurance values, inventory turn and margin per piece.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with memo exposure: what is out on loan right now and for how long.

leads.note: Founder owned American furniture house with a SoHo storefront and its own Philadelphia workshop. Made to order pieces, long lead times, deposits and freight on every order.
leads.fix: Order to cash on made to order pieces: deposits, lead time promises, workshop capacity and freight in one clean ledger with a client facing status page.
leads.open: Walk in, ask for the showroom director. Open with how many open orders are past their promised ship week and nobody can say without a spreadsheet hunt.

leads.note: Three founders, their own line plus a curated gallery program, trade heavy client list. Exactly the size where the founders still do the books on the side.
leads.fix: Trade orders, vendor master for the makers they carry, and a margin view by collection so the partners stop guessing which pieces carry the studio.
leads.open: Visit the Hudson Street showroom. Ask which collection made them the most money last year and watch how long the answer takes.

leads.note: Antique and custom carpets on Madison, family owned, serving designers and collectors. Overseas production and antique inventory under one roof.
leads.fix: Custom production tracking and antique inventory ledger with real margin per piece.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with custom order status and who calls the designer when a loom slips.

leads.note: Twentieth century European design dealer on the 10th Street strip. Founder run, high value pieces, trade clients.
leads.fix: Piece level margin and holding time, client purchase history, and a clean trade discount record.
leads.open: Walk in. Pair with the other 10th Street dealers on one route.

leads.note: Vintage and contemporary design dealer in the Fine Arts Building on East 61st, a cluster of dealers in one building.
leads.fix: Inventory ledger with margin and turn, client history, and consignment statements for the designers she represents.
leads.open: Walk the Fine Arts Building and hit several dealers in one afternoon.

leads.note: Mid century dealer in the New York Design Center. Founder run, trade clients, one of a kind inventory.
leads.fix: Inventory margin and holding time, trade client history.
leads.open: Walk in on Bond Street, two blocks from the 10th Street dealers.

leads.note: French post war design and ceramics dealer, founder run, publishes catalogues. Inventory heavy with long holding periods.
leads.fix: Inventory carry cost and turn by category, plus a clean record of provenance documents tied to each piece.
leads.open: Walk in. Ask what the carrying cost on the inventory is per month. The answer is usually a shrug.

leads.note: Art Deco and contemporary design dealer on 10th Street with two spaces. Represents living designers, so commissions and production costs sit next to antiques.
leads.fix: Two ledgers made one: antiques inventory and commissioned production, each with real margin.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with the split: which half of the business, antiques or commissions, actually funds the other.

leads.d: Zesty Meyers and Evan Snyderman, founders
leads.note: Leading design gallery with two Tribeca spaces, represented artists, art fairs and museum loans. Consignment math, fair costs and shipping on every sale.
leads.fix: Artist consignment settlements, fair by fair profitability and the shipping and insurance spend that never gets allocated to a sale.
leads.open: Walk into 64 White. Open with art fair ROI: which fairs made money after shipping, booth and travel.

leads.note: Luxury event florist famous for the Flower Flash. Event quotes, perishable purchasing, freelance labor and rentals.
leads.fix: Event P&L from quote to actual: flowers, labor, rentals and the overages that never get billed.
leads.open: Call. Open with quote versus actual on the last ten events.

leads.note: Boutique condo developer and converter, principal led, small team, large projects. Classic small team, big money.
leads.fix: Project cost control and sales reporting a small team can keep current without a controller's week.
leads.open: Call. Open with the monthly project report: who builds it and how long.

leads.d: Marisa Perry and Douglas Elliott, owners
leads.note: Owner run SoHo atelier for custom engagement rings. Every sale is a custom build with a deposit and a bench timeline.
leads.fix: Custom build tracker and deposit ledger, plus stone inventory.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with how many builds are on the bench and which are late.

leads.note: Residential management, president led, writes about boards and governance. Likes to be seen as the thoughtful manager, which fits a data proof story.
leads.fix: Board ledgers with budget versus actual and vendor spend, plus capital planning views.
leads.open: Call. Open with a board facing page he can show in his next pitch to a building.

leads.note: Family tile business since 1921 with Flatiron and other showrooms, contractor and designer customers. Volume plus custom in the same system.
leads.fix: Customer master across contractor and designer accounts, pricing control, and inventory by location.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with pricing control across the showrooms.

leads.note: Stone and tile source for architects, founder led, showrooms in several cities. Spec driven sales with long project cycles.
leads.fix: Project pipeline from spec to order, quote hit rate and the cost of samples that never convert.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with spec to order conversion by architect account.

leads.note: Alexa Hampton's studio plus licensed product lines. Owner decides, purchasing plus royalty income.
leads.fix: Purchasing ledger plus royalty and licensing income tracking.
leads.open: Call. Open with royalty statements: are they checked against anything.

leads.d: Suzanne Demisch and Stephane Danant, founders
leads.note: French mid century specialists in a Village townhouse gallery. Small team, high ticket pieces, international sourcing in euros.
leads.fix: Currency and shipping cost per piece, consignment versus owned inventory, and client follow up that is not a notebook.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with how the euro moves hit margin on pieces bought two years ago.

leads.d: Jennifer Gandia and Christina Gandia Gambale, owners
leads.note: Family owned independent jeweler, sisters run it, strong digital presence and custom work. Fine jewelry plus bridal custom orders.
leads.fix: Custom order pipeline from deposit to casting to delivery, repair tracking, and inventory by designer.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with custom order status.

leads.d: Kim Hostler and Juliet Burrows, founders
leads.note: Nordic design and contemporary ceramics, New York and LA galleries, fair program. Two founders, no finance staff beyond a bookkeeper.
leads.fix: Two city inventory and consignment ledger, fair profitability and shipping allocation.
leads.open: Walk in. Ask how a piece that moved from LA to New York to a fair gets costed. It usually does not.

leads.d: Rachel Lehmann and David Maupin, founders
leads.note: Gallery with New York, Seoul and London spaces. Multi currency, multi location inventory, heavy fair calendar.
leads.fix: Multi location inventory and consignment ledger with currency effects.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with inventory location truth across three cities.

leads.note: Family owned residential management firm for co ops and condos. Manages other people's money across dozens of buildings, boards want transparency, no IT department.
leads.fix: Board facing building ledgers: vendor spend across the portfolio, duplicate invoices, arrears, and a reserve and capital plan view each board can open.
leads.open: Call the president. Open with portfolio vendor spend: the same plumber at different prices in six buildings.

leads.note: Owner's rep and construction advisory founded by a Lehrer McGovern Bovis founder. Deep credibility, small firm, institutional clients.
leads.fix: Owner ledger and claims ready cost record.
leads.open: Warm intro preferred. Open with the data behind claims: who can prove the number.

leads.note: Owner's representative for institutions, nonprofits and private owners. Manages other people's construction money, small firm, reports to boards.
leads.fix: Owner facing project ledger: budget, commitments, change orders, pay app checks and schedule, the same product proven with PGM.
leads.open: Call. Open with the PGM owner ledger as a reference. Same business, same pain.

leads.note: Ultra high end boutique brokerage, founder led, celebrity and family office clientele. Confidentiality is the product.
leads.fix: Private client database and deal pipeline with real confidentiality controls, marketing spend by listing, and co broke economics.
leads.open: Warm intro preferred. Open with confidentiality: a client ledger nobody outside the firm can see, hosted on our own infrastructure.

leads.note: Third generation dealer in rare jewels, by appointment on Fifth Avenue. Very small team, very high ticket.
leads.fix: Inventory ledger with provenance, holding cost and client history.
leads.open: Book an appointment. Open with holding cost.

leads.note: High society event design, founder led, custom builds and vendor orchestration for every event.
leads.fix: Event budget ledger with vendor commitments and client facing budget page.
leads.open: Warm intro preferred. Open with the client budget page.

leads.note: Upper East Side co op and condo manager, family owned, high end buildings. Smaller team, older systems.
leads.fix: Board ledger and vendor spend, built so a small team can run it.
leads.open: Call. Open with how long it takes to answer a board treasurer's question about a vendor.

leads.note: Owner's rep for cultural institutions, schools and private clients. Reports to boards and donors, small team, high stakes.
leads.fix: Board ready project ledger with change order and pay app control, refreshed from the CM's data.
leads.open: Call. Open with board reporting on capital projects.

leads.note: Luxury retail and residential design studio, founder led, flagship clients worldwide.
leads.fix: Fee realization and FF&E ledger with client facing reporting.
leads.open: Warm intro preferred.

leads.note: Luxury residential GC working with the top interior designers. Many open projects, many subs.
leads.fix: Project cost control and client facing ledger.
leads.open: Call. Lead with the cost plus client page.

leads.d: Gabriel Hendifar, founder and creative director
leads.note: Founder led lighting and furniture house with its own New York production. Growing fast, international dealers, bespoke finishes. Big enough to leak, small enough to have no data team.
leads.fix: Quote to cash for bespoke lighting: finish options, dealer discounts, production scheduling and the margin on each configured piece.
leads.open: Book a visit through the site. Open with configured product margin: which finish combinations lose money after rework.

leads.note: Boutique developer of design led condos and hotels in Manhattan and the Jersey Shore. Founder led, small team.
leads.fix: Multi project cost ledger and lender reporting pack built from clean draw data.
leads.open: Call. Open with lender draw packages: hours per draw and errors caught late.

leads.note: Owner's rep for museums, galleries and high end residential. Cultural clients want transparency to boards.
leads.fix: Owner ledger with change orders and pay app validation.
leads.open: Call. Lead with the owner ledger and Jake's validation sign off.

leads.note: Large residential design studio with its own purchasing and expediting team. Hundreds of vendors, high value projects, founder led.
leads.fix: Purchasing and expediting ledger with vendor performance, deposit exposure and project margin.
leads.open: Call. Open with vendor performance: who ships late and what it costs the studio in expediting hours.

leads.note: Founder led brokerage with a FiDi office and a tech forward posture. Sales and rentals, agent training programs.
leads.fix: Agent productivity, lead source ROI and commission settlement in one place.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with lead source ROI: which portals actually produce closed deals per dollar.

leads.note: Architecture practice for museums, galleries and private houses. Principal led, long projects, consultant heavy budgets.
leads.fix: Project fee and consultant budget ledger with phase level realization.
leads.open: Call. Open with consultant budget versus fee by phase.

leads.d: Jesse Carrier and Mara Miller, partners
leads.note: Residential design studio, two partners, high profile clients. Purchasing on behalf of clients.
leads.fix: Purchasing ledger with deposit exposure and vendor performance.
leads.open: Call. Open with deposit exposure.

leads.d: Jamie Drake and Caleb Anderson, partners
leads.note: Top tier residential design studio, two partners. Every project is purchasing on the client's behalf: deposits, vendor POs, freight, receiving, installation.
leads.fix: Design purchasing ledger: client deposits versus vendor POs versus received goods, with margin on product and a client facing status page.
leads.open: Call the studio director. Open with open POs versus client deposits: how much client money is out with vendors right now.

leads.d: Partners, Marc Turkel and Morgan Hare
leads.note: Architecture and interiors studio with a nonprofit arm. Partners decide.
leads.fix: Fee realization and consultant ledger.
leads.open: Call.

leads.d: Brian Sawyer and John Berson, partners
leads.note: Architecture, landscape and interiors for private estates. Partners decide, long projects, big budgets.
leads.fix: Project fee and purchasing ledger across three disciplines with client facing reporting.
leads.open: Call. Open with fee realization by phase across disciplines.

leads.note: Family owned tile and stone house with a Flatiron flagship and several regional showrooms. Many SKUs, imports, slab inventory. Bigger than the sweet spot but still family decided.
leads.fix: Slab and SKU inventory truth, landed cost, and quote accuracy across showrooms.
leads.open: Walk in. Open with quote accuracy: how often the installed cost beats the quoted cost and why.

leads.note: Fast growing brokerage with a SoHo storefront and its own AI assistant for agents. Loud about AI, which is good for the conversation, but it is already building in house and well past the size band.
leads.fix: Data cleansing behind the AI: listing, client and transaction master data at a stated confidence before the models touch it.
leads.open: Walk into the SoHo studio. Open with the data under the AI: what confidence level is the listing and client data at. Watch lead.

leads.d: Matt Berman and Andrew Kotchen, founders
leads.note: Architecture and interiors studio with its own product lines and a tech friendly posture. Founders decide.
leads.fix: Studio fee ledger plus product line margin, with a client facing project page.
leads.open: Call. Open with product line margin next to studio fees.

leads.d: Sarah Saltzberg, co founder and CEO
leads.note: Upper Manhattan brokerage with storefront offices, founder led, heavy rental volume. Many small transactions, many agents, thin margins.
leads.fix: Rental deal flow and agent commission settlement, landlord client master, and listing marketing cost per lease.
leads.open: Walk into the Harlem storefront. Open with commission settlement speed and error rate.

leads.d: Principals, Paul Wolf and Jonathan Denham
leads.note: Real estate and project management for nonprofits. Clients are boards with grant and donor money, exactly where transparency sells.
leads.fix: Nonprofit board facing project ledger with funding source tracking against spend.
leads.open: Call. Open with funding source to spend tracking on capital projects.

leads.note: Townhouse and mixed use building specialists since 1972, family run, roughly 40 agents. Publishes its own townhouse market reports, so data already matters here.
leads.fix: Townhouse sales database cleaned and completed, agent production and marketing spend per listing, and a client facing market report engine.
leads.open: Call for a meeting, then visit. Open with the townhouse report: we can turn it from a PDF into a live page their clients log into.

leads.note: Family owned manager and owner with a published technology posture and a resident app. Already believes in tech, no data team.
leads.fix: Data layer under the resident app: vendor, unit and work order master data cleaned and completed, with board and owner dashboards.
leads.open: Call. Open with the gap between the resident app and what boards actually see about money.

leads.note: Classic Upper East Side residential design and art advisory, partner led. High value purchasing on behalf of clients.
leads.fix: Purchasing ledger and client facing status page.
leads.open: Call. Same purchasing pitch as Drake/Anderson.

leads.note: Design driven developer that also builds and designs in house. Vertically integrated, so cost data crosses three disciplines.
leads.fix: One cost ledger across development, design and construction arms with change order and pay app control.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting. Open with pay app accuracy: the one to three percent that slips through.

leads.note: Brokerage that markets itself on data and analytics for buyers. Founder led, luxury tier, open to technology by positioning.
leads.fix: The analytics they advertise, built on cleaned and completed listing data with a confidence score, plus client facing market pages.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting. Open with data confidence: how complete is the comp set behind the reports agents send.

leads.note: Residential management for high end co ops and condos, principal led, long tenure clients. Classic manages other people's money profile.
leads.fix: Portfolio vendor spend analysis and a board facing ledger per building.
leads.open: Call. Open with vendor consolidation across the portfolio.

leads.note: High end residential construction manager for designers and private clients. Cost plus, allowances and change orders.
leads.fix: Cost plus client ledger with allowances and change orders.
leads.open: Call. Same pitch as Taconic.

leads.note: Luxury residential developer, founder led, several Manhattan condo projects at once. Hard costs, soft costs, change orders and sales velocity across projects.
leads.fix: Project cost ledger across developments: budget versus committed versus paid, change orders, and a sales velocity view per building.
leads.open: Warm intro preferred. Open with change order exposure across active projects.

leads.note: Hospitality and residential design studio with a global client base. Partner led, big FF&E budgets handled through purchasing agents.
leads.fix: FF&E budget tracking against purchasing agent reports, with a client facing budget page.
leads.open: Call. Open with FF&E budget drift between concept and install.

leads.d: Will Meyer and Gray Davis, founders
leads.note: Hospitality, retail and residential design studio, two founders. Project fee realization and FF&E oversight.
leads.fix: Fee realization and FF&E oversight ledger.
leads.open: Call. Open with fee realization by project type.

leads.note: Hospitality design firm with its own restaurants and product brands. Partners run multiple businesses off one back office.
leads.fix: One ledger across design fees, product brands and operating restaurants.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting. Open with the back office that serves three businesses.

leads.note: Co op and condo management, principal led, Flatiron office. Boards and monthly reporting.
leads.fix: Board ledger and portfolio vendor spend.
leads.open: Call. Same board package pitch as Orsid and Gumley Haft.

leads.note: Founder led boutique brokerage with storefront offices and a new development marketing arm. Shaun Osher is vocal on technology and brand. More agents than the sweet spot, one decision maker.
leads.fix: New development sales velocity and marketing spend per unit, agent productivity, and clean building and unit master data across listings.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting with Shaun Osher's team. Open with marketing spend per signed contract on new development.

leads.d: Karla Saladino, co founder and managing partner
leads.note: Rental and sales brokerage known for leasing new developments for landlords. Landlord reporting is part of the service, so a client facing dashboard sells itself.
leads.fix: Landlord facing leasing dashboard: units, days on market, concessions, net effective rent, agent performance.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting. Open with landlord reporting: replace the weekly email with a live page per building.

leads.d: Principals, Neil Davidowitz and Dennis DePaola
leads.note: Luxury co op and condo manager with a reputation for white glove boards. Boards are demanding, reporting is monthly and manual.
leads.fix: Board portal with budget versus actual, vendor spend, arrears and capital projects, refreshed from the accounting system.
leads.open: Ask for a meeting with a principal. Open with the board package: hours to produce it and how often a board asks a question nobody can answer in the room.

leads.d: Founder led, James Hanley and Michael Hanley
leads.note: High end residential builder for the top designers and architects. Cost plus contracts, hundreds of subs, demanding clients who want to see every dollar.
leads.fix: Client facing cost plus ledger: subs, allowances, change orders and markups in one page the client can open.
leads.open: Call. Open with the cost plus client who asks for the backup binder. Give them a page instead.

leads.note: Architecture and interiors firm, founder led, many Manhattan buildings. Larger team but one principal.
leads.fix: Fee realization and staffing utilization by project.
leads.open: Call. Open with utilization versus fee realization.

leads.note: Luxury residential contractor, founder led, known for process and client communication. Bigger than the sweet spot, but one owner who values the client experience.
leads.fix: Client facing project ledger and schedule page, plus sub and vendor spend analysis across projects.
leads.open: Call. Open with the client page: budget, schedule, selections, in plain English.

leads.d: Brand owned flagship, local general manager
leads.note: Italian kitchen and bath flagship. Brand owned, so the decision sits partly in Italy. Good door to learn the kitchen project cycle, lower odds of a quick yes.
leads.fix: Kitchen project tracking from deposit to install, change orders and installer payments.
leads.open: Walk in to learn the project cycle. Treat as a Watch lead.

leads.note: Public brokerage with its own engineering and data teams. Loud about AI, already built.
leads.fix: Not a fit. In house engineering.
leads.open: Skip.

leads.note: Corporate retail chain. Decisions in Michigan, not on the floor.
leads.fix: Not a fit.
leads.open: Skip.

leads.note: Beautiful showroom, but owned by MillerKnoll with corporate finance and BI teams. Not our buyer.
leads.fix: Not a fit. Corporate parent owns the data function.
leads.open: Skip. Walk through for market knowledge only.

leads.note: Established Chelsea gallery with several spaces on 27th Street. Estates and living artists, fairs, publishing.
leads.fix: Consignment and estate settlements, fair P&L.
leads.open: Walk in.

leads.note: International project and cost consultancy with its own data practice. Competes with us on reporting.
leads.fix: Not a fit. Competitor as much as client.
leads.open: Skip.

routes.name: SoHo and Tribeca design row
routes.blurb: Founder owned showrooms and dealers within a 20 minute walk of each other. Best first day: every door opens to the public.

routes.name: 10th Street dealers and the Village
routes.blurb: Six dealers on two blocks of East 10th plus Bond Street. One afternoon, same pitch each door: inventory margin and consignment math.

routes.name: Flatiron, NoMad and Chelsea trade
routes.blurb: Tile and stone houses, the Madison showrooms and the Chelsea design studios. Mix of walk in and call first.

routes.name: Chelsea galleries
routes.blurb: Gallery row is open Tuesday to Saturday. Ask for the director, open with fair P&L and consignment settlements.

routes.name: Upper East Side and 59th Street
routes.blurb: The Fine Arts Building at 306 East 61st holds three dealers in one elevator ride. Add the A&D Building and Madison Avenue.

routes.name: Midtown owners and managers
routes.blurb: Call first. Property managers, owner's reps and developers whose clients are boards. Lead with the PGM owner ledger.

routes.name: Upper West Side and Harlem
routes.blurb: Two call first stops north of the park line. Pair with an Upper East Side day.

routes.name: Downtown owners and studios
routes.blurb: FiDi and Hudson Square offices. Owner's reps, builders and design studios. Call first, pair with route one.

bdny.name: BDNY 2026
bdny.note: 861 exhibitors on the a2z floor plan. Most are national and overseas manufacturers with their own sales and finance teams, which is not our buyer. The list below is the New York based, owner led slice worth a booth conversation, plus the three radar firms that are exhibiting.

new.why: Family owned rug house in the New York Design Center. One of a kind inventory, trade pricing, consignment to designers.
new.open: Which rugs have been out on approval longer than 60 days, and what is tied up in them.

new.why: Owner run rug dealer, residential and hospitality, same building as Bokara.
new.open: Approval and memo tracking, plus landed cost on imports.

new.why: Small leather house selling to designers and hotel FF&E. Hides priced by the square foot, lots of custom.

play: Walk the New York cluster first

Bokara 1268, Rug & Kilim 1133, Mosaique 1156, ArtStar 1164, Ngala 1146 and Reid Witlin 255E are within a few aisles of each other in the low numbers. Start there Sunday morning before the hotel buyers arrive.
Lead with their numbers, not ours

Booth staff want to sell product. Ask the owner question from the card: open orders past promised date, approvals out over 60 days, landed cost versus quote. If the owner is not in the booth, get the owner's name and leave.
Stone Source, Artistic Tile and Nemo are already on the radar with openers. The booth is the easiest version of the walk in: nobody is behind a desk.
Most of the 861 are national manufacturers with finance teams. The Azorian3 filter still applies on the floor: owner led, 5 to 50 people, no data team.
Everyone you meet gets the same note Tuesday morning: the one number you asked about and a 20 minute screen share offer on fake data. Log each in the status tracker.
